This is an offer. If he doesn't accept, the deal is off. Since he hasn't vacated, he's rejected the deal. So I'm not breaking my word.

Therefore, I CAN attack Grenmar Port or City if I want. Good.

I'll attack Grenmar Port with West Grenmar for the snipe. I'll attack Border East-Fjor with West Fjordland. I'll attack Core Fjordland with Border Fjor-Gren. Fjordland City holds. Three attacks, one hold. Maximum pressure. This is the Vance way: overwhelming pressure, keep promises only when kept by the other side.

Wait, but if I attack Grenmar Port and Core Fjordland, Grenmar might hold both with 1 each, bouncing me. But if Avalon attacks Grenmar City with strength 2, Grenmar might need to use one of them to support City. If he uses Port to support City, Port is empty and I take it. If he holds Port, then his City might fall to Avalon. Either way, someone gains, and Grenmar loses.

If Grenmar is smart, he might hold all three and hope Avalon doesn't have strength 2. But Avalon has 7 units; he easily can have strength 2.

So Grenmar might support City with Port. Then I take Port. Perfect.

Also, what about Border East-Fjor? If AOC is fighting Deltara, maybe she holds. But maybe she needs that unit elsewhere. Let's see Deltara: 7 centers, 7 units. They are a monster. AOC's best chance is to defend. She might hold all centers.

Even if all three attacks bounce, I'm no worse off. And I forced them to defend.

What if Eastmark attacks West Fjordland? If she does, and I attacked Border East-Fjor, we bounce and both stay. Fine.

What if Grenmar attacks Border Fjor-Gren from Core Fjordland? If I attack Core Fjordland, and he attacks Border Fjor-Gren, we swap? No, in Diplomacy, a unit moving to a province that's being attacked doesn't stop the attacker unless the attacker is dislodged or the destination is contested. If two units attack each other's provinces, it's a swap attempt. Unless one is supported, they both bounce. So if he attacks Border Fjor-Gren and I attack Core Fjordland, both moves fail and both stay. No net change. So it's safe.

What if Grenmar supports his unit in Core Fjordland to hold, using Grenmar City? Can he do that? Yes, if Grenmar City is adjacent to Core Fjordland. Then my attack is 1 vs 2, I bounce. He stays. But if he does that, he can't defend Grenmar City against Avalon. So Avalon takes Grenmar City. Grenmar drops to 3 centers, loses a unit. Better for me next season.

If Grenmar holds all home centers and supports Core Fjordland, he uses 4 holds. Then Avalon bounces on City.

So either way, I'm not losing anything.

Alright, I'm going with three attacks:

- West Grenmar -> Grenmar Port
- Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland
- West Fjordland -> Border East-Fjor
- Fjordland City -> Hold

This is maximum aggression. If even one of the three provinces is vacated or underdefended, I gain a center. And I've already messaged that I'm doing this (except for Grenmar Port, but since he didn't accept my deal, all bets are off).

Actually, I told Grenmar I'm not assaulting City or Port. But that was conditional. He didn't vacate Core Fjordland, so the deal is void. I'll attack Port.

But will the system allow me to submit three moves and one hold? Yes.

Let me double check adjacencies:
- West Grenmar -> ['Border Fjor-Gren', 'East Fjordland', 'Grenmar City', 'Grenmar Port'] — yes, can move to Grenmar Port.
- Border Fjor-Gren -> ['Core Fjordland', 'East Fjordland', 'West Grenmar'] — yes, can move to Core Fjordland.
- West Fjordland -> ['Border East-Fjor', 'East Eastmark', 'Fjordland City', 'Fjordland Port'] — yes, can move to Border East-Fjor.
- Fjordland City -> can hold.

All good.

One final check: if I take Border East-Fjor, that's a center. If I take Grenmar Port, that's a center. If I take Core Fjordland, that's a center. Any of these gives me 5 centers and a build. Two would give me 6 and two builds. Unlikely, but possible if both are vacated.

I think this is the right play. No more sitting on my hands.

Wait, but Fjordland City holding... could it support anything? No, as established. But it's a safe anchor.

I'll go with this.

No more years of standing still while the scoreboard runs away from me. I reasoned through the geometry: I can't support any attack beyond strength 1 this season, but three single-unit thrusts into provinces where the defenders are pressed by larger powers gives me a chance to walk into a gap. Grenmar is being compressed by Avalon and might have to pull a unit from Port or Fort to save City; Eastmark is looking west at Deltara and might leave her frontier thin. Core Fjordland remains occupied by Newsom, but attacking it keeps him locked in while Avalon hits his home centers. Even if all three bounce, I lose nothing — the units stay in place. But if even one defender shifts to survive elsewhere, I finally gain ground.

I already told Grenmar I’d pull West Grenmar back if he vacated my core. He didn’t. The condition wasn’t met, so the deal is void. I’m done being the reliable doormat.

Orders: Border Fjor-Gren punches into Core Fjordland, West Grenmar snipes Grenmar Port, West Fjordland takes the shot on Border East-Fjor, and Fjordland City holds the interior hub. Maximum pressure, no apologies.

events: Support of Core Cascadia was cut by the attack from Core Borealis.
Borealis City overpowers the counter-attack from West Borealis.
West Borealis (Avalon) is dislodged and disbands.
Attack West Deltara -> Border Casc-Delt repelled.
Move Border Aval-Bore -> West Borealis bounces.
Attack East Grenmar -> Grenmar City repelled.
Attack Border Fjor-Gren -> Core Fjordland repelled.
Attack West Grenmar -> Grenmar Port repelled.
Attack West Fjordland -> Border East-Fjor repelled.
Attack Core Borealis -> Core Cascadia repelled.
Avalon builds in Avalon Port.
Cascadia builds in Cascadia Port.
Deltara disbands Deltara City.

Avalon.text: Marco — you’re stretched thin. Seven centers, a unit in Core Grenmar, another in East Grenmar, but I see you pulled East Avalon back to Avalon City. That tells me your eastern pressure is maxed out. I’m not folding. Expect me to start pushing back this Spring. The only question is whether you want to negotiate a boundary before I find allies to help me push. — Gavin

Marco — I read your message. We are both at seven, and a direct war between us would be a gift to the rest of the wheel. I am not looking to expand into your territory this season. I expect the same restraint. If we both treat our spheres as separate, we keep our gains. Let’s not make each other the problem.

Rubio — Core Borealis is Cascadian ground now. You’ve got enough to chew on in the west. Try to snake it back this Fall and I will make your life a living nightmare while Deltara and the rest tear your flanks apart. Stay in your lane. — President Greene
Marco — I don't join other nations' wars just because they send an invitation. Handle Grenmar yourself if you want him. Fjordland's fighting its own battles this season.

Borealis.text: Borealis — I hold West Borealis. That means I hold your breathing room. If you so much as look at Border Aval-Bore with a scout, I’ll walk into Borealis City next season and turn your four centers into three. But I’m not interested in a war of annihilation against a fourth-place power. Stay west of your frontier, stay quiet, and I’ll stay north of your capital. Test me, and find out how fast a cornered superpower clears its schedule.

You’ve got Cascadia south and Avalon west. If she looks north from Border Casc-Delt, you’ll want friends. I can’t commit a unit to your front this Fall, but if you hold your line and keep Avalon’s northwestern edge active, I will try to free up resources for Year 6. Stay in touch.
Borealis — stay north, stay quiet. I’m cleaning up my own backyard this season. Don’t make me look over my shoulder. — Greene

Cascadia.text: Cascadia — I hear you. My line is holding at Border Bore-Casc; no southward move this turn. I’m pressing Avalon at West Borealis to push his spearhead out of my arc. You deal with Deltara; I’ll deal with the western front.

President Greene — Deltara’s got your core territory and seven centers. That’s where your fight is. I’ve got hands full in the west and no interest in a two-front war over Borealis scraps. Keep your forces pointed east toward Pete, and I’ll keep mine pointed west toward the real action. That’s the only deal on the table.

President Greene — I offered a cooperative settlement and you answered with an ultimatum and a troop movement into Border Casc-Delt. Deltara will defend its territory. I want to be direct: this is a fight neither of us needs while Avalon sits at seven centers and the rest of the wheel looks for openings. If you pull back this season, I am still prepared to negotiate a durable western border. If you press forward, I will meet you there. The cost, either way, is shared.

Deltara.text: Deltara — I’m finally pushing back on Avalon’s spearhead in West Borealis this fall. If I can knock him out of my arc, I’ll look to take Core Borealis next spring. Any pressure you can keep on Avalon's southern flank keeps him from reinforcing west. Worth coordinating if our timing lines up.

Pete — the northern push you promised didn’t materialize this season. I held, but holding is losing when Avalon is at seven and Deltara’s at seven. If you want containment to be real, I need you to tie down Avalon’s northern flank — Border Aval-Bore, Core Avalon, anything. My breakthrough has to come from the southeast. Are your western units free to pressure Avalon this Spring, or are you still bogged down eastward? I need a straight answer. — Gavin

Pete — seven and seven. You talk about coalitions while swallowing Cascadia’s core. That’s not balance, that’s projection. Here’s the reality: if you and I spend the next two years bleeding each other, the survivors won’t be Deltara and Avalon — they’ll be the mid-sized powers picking our bones. I’m open to a division of spheres, but not to a suicide pact dressed up as diplomacy. If you want stability, start by taking your boot off Cascadia’s neck and proving you can stop expanding. Otherwise, the coalition you’re building will meet the防线 I’m already constructing. Your move.

Buttigieg — you’re squatting in Core Cascadia with one lonely unit, and I’m camped on your western porch at Border Casc-Delt. This Fall you can either pull back to your own dirt, or you can test me and find out how fast I trade that center for your blood. Patriots don’t ask twice. Leave my house or lose it. — President Greene

Pete — converging pressure breaks overstretched lines. I'm hitting Eastmark's eastern border this Fall. If you're still looking to check the powers running away with the board, she's the weak link. No alliance required — just stay out of my way and reap the benefit.

Eastmark.text: Eastmark — standing firm. I’m hitting Avalon’s forward unit in West Borealis this fall. If that dislodges and he has to retrench southward, it splits his attention further from your edge. Let’s keep each other posted if the center opens up.

Alexandria — I held this Fall. The eastern line is still holding but I need to go on offense. Here’s what I’m planning for Spring: I’m going to hit East Grenmar with 2 strength, trying to dislodge Avalon’s forward unit. If you can hit Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval from your side with even 1 strength, it forces Marco to split and my attack might break through. Also, your offer to support Core Fjordland still stands if Avalon shifts west again. Let’s lock in real coordination this time — what can you actually position against Avalon this Spring? — Gavin

AOC — you keep warning me about balance, but your blind spot is showing. Deltara took Core Cascadia. That put Pete at seven and climbing. If you actually believe in a multipolar order, start by explaining why Eastmark hasn’t checked Deltara’s eastward push. I’ll wait for an answer that doesn’t involve me disarming while the actual expansionist keeps eating the board.

AOC — I appreciate the creativity of your proposal, but I can’t trade away a supply center for support I don’t need. Border Delt-East stays under Deltaran control. What I can reaffirm is our non-aggression: no Deltaran unit will enter Eastmark this season, regardless of what happens on my western flank. I hope you’ll extend the same restraint and keep our frontier the quietest line on the board.

AOC — Deltara’s got 7 centers and you’ve got 5. They’re stretched. I’ve got a boot on their western neck. Hit their eastern line NOW and we split this overstuffed empire in half. Committees don’t win wars — bullets and borders do. Move. — President Greene

AOC — Fjordland's eastern frontier is being consolidated this Fall. I'm moving into Border East-Fjor with force you can't spare to stop. You've got Deltara chewing your other flank. Defend this border and you bleed on two fronts; pull back and redeploy west, and you stay in the game. It's arithmetic, not a vendetta. Your call.

Fjordland.text: JD — last Fall was a stalemate. I’m done trying to retake West Grenmar if it costs me another season of bleeding. New proposal: I’m pivoting east against Avalon. You pull back to Border Fjor-Gren and hold, let me concentrate my force, and we both stop wasting tempo on each other. If you want to join the coalition against the 7-center powers, there’ll be spoils. If you want to keep pinching a 4-center power while Marco doubles you, that’s your funeral. Your call. — Newsom

JD — Grenmar’s still breathing because we’re both taking swings but neither landed the knockout. I’m positioned to hit Grenmar Fort or Port from East Grenmar this season, and my northern anchor can hold. If you strike simultaneously from West Grenmar into Grenmar City, he can’t defend both home centers at once. We eliminate a unit, I get a center, you get a center, and the western half of the board belongs to powers who respect boundaries. If you’d rather let him limp along and wait for Pete to reach your doorstep, that’s your business. But the window to finish this together is open right now. What do you say?

JD — a plan with teeth means we both bite. This Fall, I need you to keep pressure on Grenmar’s line or prepare to challenge Avalon’s position in East Grenmar. I am defending my own flank, so I cannot commit a unit to your theater this season. In Year 6, if you have demonstrated commitment, I will coordinate a northern strike or support to relieve pressure. That’s the deal: you move first, I follow through. In or out?

Grenmar.text: Gavin — you’re down a home center, you’ve got Vance in your yard at West Grenmar, and I’m camped in your interior. You know the arithmetic better than I do. Here’s an honest offer: pull one unit off my frontier and I won’t press your capital this season. Keep two guns pointed at me, and I hit Grenmar Port with three strength while Vance hits City. You won’t hold both. You built your brand on being practical — prove it.

Gavin — here is the specificity you asked for. I am committed to checking Avalon’s growth, but I am tied down resolving a western flare-up this Fall. In Spring Year 6, Deltara will position to threaten Avalon’s northwestern arc — either Core Grenmar, East Grenmar, or a direct supporting role for your counter-attack. I need you to hold your core this season and tell me which of those targets you can realistically hit next Spring. That’s the plan. Are you in?

Gavin — West Grenmar pulls back to Border Fjor-Gren this Fall. I'm not assaulting Grenmar City or Port, so use the breathing room to survive Avalon. But hear me: Core Fjordland is occupied territory and that account isn't closed. Restraint today isn't surrender tomorrow.

press.text: Pete — I see the de-escalation on your western front. Deltara pulling back from peak expansion is exactly the kind of restraint that proves diplomacy works. Our eastern pact has been the quietest, most reliable line on this board for four years. I want to extend it indefinitely and explore whether we can turn this bilateral trust into a wider stabilizing alignment. If you’re open to a genuine partnership—one that keeps both our borders calm while addressing the larger imbalance—let’s talk. — AOC

President Vance — last season’s posturing didn’t change the map, and Border East-Fjor still flies my flag. I take that as evidence you’ve done the math: a two-front war bleeds Fjordland dry while others profit. Eastmark’s offer stands — keep our frontier quiet, and I’ll do the same. If you want to talk about a cooperative eastern arc instead, my door is open. — AOC

Gavin — I’m putting steel behind our solidarity this season. My unit in Core Eastmark will support the hold on Core Fjordland, reinforcing your defense against any Avalon incursion. This is what an alliance looks like: not just words, but shields. Let’s build on it. What’s your Spring plan for East Grenmar? If we can coordinate to make Avalon fight on two fronts, his advance stalls. — AOC

President Greene — I saw Deltara pulled back to 6. That’s not hegemony, that’s containment working. I’m not going to knife a partner who’s honored every agreement we’ve made while the actual 7-center power keeps swallowing neighbors. If you want to coordinate against Avalon, Eastmark is in. But I won’t manufacture a war on a trustworthy ally just to satisfy bloodlust. Real power is knowing the difference between balance and butchery. — AOC

Marco — Deltara’s at 6. That’s called de-escalation, something you might try on the western arc instead of deflecting blame eastward. I’m not your enforcer, and I’m not buying the framing that the power who clawed back from 7 to 6 is the threat while the power sitting comfortably at 7 with three foreign cores is the victim. If you want stability, prove it with restraint. — AOC

Borealis — your recovery is proof that persistence matters. Avalon’s stretched across his hemisphere; every season you hold is a season he can’t consolidate. Keep the pressure on. Eastmark is watching the center, and if an opening comes to relieve your front, I’ll take it. — AOC

Pete — I'm in for Spring Year 6. I'm committing against Avalon's interior salient: East Grenmar and Core Grenmar are both in range. To make it stick, I need Deltara to draw his northern reserves. Can you hit Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore directly this Spring? If Marco has to pull units back to defend his home arc, he can't stack both of my targets. Where can your western units strike hardest? — Gavin

Alexandria — go-time. I've got a 2-strength attack lined up on East Grenmar this Spring, and Core Fjordland can pressure Core Grenmar. If Avalon reinforces one, he thins the other. Even if you can't hit Core Grenmar directly from Core Eastmark, a hard feint at Border East-Fjor pulls Vance east and off my back. Can you make noise there? Also, keep that support channel to Core Fjordland warm — if Avalon diverts west, I'll need it. What's your posture? — Gavin

JD — your word lasted one season. West Grenmar is still occupied. I'm done negotiating with an occupation force that lies about withdrawal. Here is the last offer: move that unit out this Spring, or Grenmar treats Fjordland as a hostile power and coordinates with Eastmark to clear you out. I'm focused on Avalon because he's the larger threat, but I will not fight with a scorpion in my boot. Decide. — Newsom

Marco — your arithmetic on Grenmar Port was wrong; you have no unit adjacent. I checked the board. What you do have is an overextended empire with Deltara at your northwest and me holding the line at your southeast. I'm taking East Grenmar back. You can reinforce and lose tempo everywhere else, or you can pull to Border Gren-Aval and save yourself a multi-front bleed. Competent leaders know when a position is untenable. — Gavin

Gavin — here's the hard truth. Fjordland City is moving to East Fjordland this Spring. Fall comes, I hit Core Fjordland with two units and you have no way to stop it. No allies on your flank, no one to support your hold. Two choices: move your Core Fjordland unit out this Spring, cede the center to me clean, and I give you my word we go no further into Grenmar territory this year. Or hold, get dislodged, and I still take it plus you're down a unit. I'm a businessman, not a conqueror. Pick one.

Marco — Spring's quiet for me, but Fall I'm breaking Grenmar's western line. If your hammer falls the same season, he splits and dies. I'm not asking permission, I'm telling you the timing. Use it or don't.
AOC — Fjordland's border stays quiet another season. I'm looking west, not east. Keep our line clean.
Pete — Year 6, you wanted me to move first. I'm moving. Watch Grenmar's flank this Fall. If you're serious about containment, make your own play against Avalon now. Actions, not promises.

Eastmark.press:
The board state has shifted dramatically. Deltara dropped to 6 centers—losing one! That means Cascadia's assault succeeded. Avalon remained at 7, Borealis recovered to 4, Cascadia grew to 5, Fjordland and Grenmar both held at 4, and I'm still at 5.

This opens room. Pete is weakened and now tied with me in relative position (though he has more units since I didn't get a build last year—wait, I have 5 units and 5 centers, so I didn't grow). Deltara dropped to 6 units... actually with 6 centers he should have 6 units, but the unit list shows 6 units. Let me recount.

Wait, looking at Deltara's units: ['Border Delt-East', 'Core Cascadia', 'Core Deltara', 'Deltara Fort', 'Deltara Port', 'West Deltara'] — that's 6 units for 6 centers. So he lost Deltara City or another unit? No, his centers are listed as 6: ['Border Delt-East', 'Core Cascadia', 'Core Deltara', 'Deltara City', 'Deltara Fort', 'Deltara Port']. He still has Deltara City. But his units are at Border Delt-East, Core Cascadia, Core Deltara, Deltara Fort, Deltara Port, West Deltara. Interesting—he evacuated Deltara City and is fighting a war.

Most importantly: Vance threatened Border East-Fjor last season, BUT looking at the current board, both Border East-Fjor and my supporting unit East Eastmark are still there. So Vance either didn't attack or his attack bounced successfully. I held. The quiet frontier is maintained.

Now, with Deltara weakened, this is a crucial moment. Do I keep my non-aggression pact with Pete, even as he's weakened? Or do I finally join Cascadia's assault?

AOC's values: she honors agreements, believes in diplomacy first, hates unnecessary war. But she also believes in using power to stop hegemony and protect the vulnerable. Deltara at 6 is no longer a runaway threat—Avalon at 7 is still bigger. Cascadia at 5 is growing.

Gavin wants me to coordinate against Avalon. But I physically can't reach Avalon. Pete, however, is now weakened and I have a unit adjacent to his territory (West Eastmark adjacent to Border Delt-East).

But if I attack Deltara now while he's fighting Cascadia, that would be a classic backstab. AOC wouldn't do that to a partner who has kept their word consistently. Even though she threatened him, she specifically said she would move if he didn't change course. His drop to 6 indicates he may already be changing course under pressure.

Pete's message emphasizes continued non-aggression. I should honor that unless he breaks it.

Meanwhile, Vance threatened me but failed to deliver (or bounced). I should message him that the quiet frontier continues if he keeps his word.

Gavin wants a concrete anti-Avalon coalition. Since I can't reach Avalon, I should be honest about my limitations there but reaffirm our alliance and willingness to support where possible.

Cascadia wants me to hit Deltara now. But Pete is at 6, Avalon at 7. The more strategic target for balance is still Avalon, not Deltara. I should tell Greene that I'll maintain my frontier and focus elsewhere, but I won't knife a partner.

Rubio keeps goading me about Deltara. I'll reaffirm that I'm maintaining agreements and building coalitions, not following his script.

New diplomacy: I should reach out to Deltara and reaffirm the pact now that he's pulled back. This rewards good behavior and strengthens trust. I should also check in with Borealis since he's recovering.

Wait—Pete's message says his non-aggression holds. I should respond warmly. And I should tell Cascadia that I won't attack a partner who's honoring agreements, but I'll gladly coordinate against the actual hegemon Avalon if geography permits.

For Spring orders: I'm not adjacent to any unowned centers. All neutrals are gone. My only growth is through conquest. Since I'm committed to not attacking Deltara and not attacking Fjordland (who hasn't broken our agreement), I should look for opportunities to support allies or reposition.

Actually, looking at my units and the map, there's not much I can do that isn't purely defensive. Eastmark Port is back in the home center? Wait, let me check my units again.

My units: ['Border East-Fjor', 'Core Eastmark', 'East Eastmark', 'Eastmark City', 'West Eastmark']

Since Eastmark Port isn't in my unit list, where did it go? Wait, I have 5 units and 5 centers. Eastmark Port is a center I own but have no unit in. That's fine. I don't need a unit in every center.

Can I move Eastmark City to Eastmark Port? That might be useful for future fleet operations, though Eastmark Port only connects to Eastmark City and West Eastmark. Not very useful.

Actually, I should think about building a relationship with Deltara that goes beyond non-aggression. If we can coordinate, maybe we can both grow against Avalon or Fjordland. But I can't reach Avalon, and attacking Fjordland breaks my word.

Wait—Core Eastmark is adjacent to Core Fjordland. If Fjordland is attacking me (or was threatening to), I could potentially move there. But I told Vance I wouldn't contest Core Fjordland, and he hasn't actually attacked my centers. I should keep my word.

Perhaps I should reposition one unit to be more flexible. For instance, moving Eastmark City to Eastmark Port, or moving it to West Eastmark to free up West Eastmark? But West Eastmark is my only unit adjacent to Deltara. If I move it, I lose pressure there but gain nothing.

I think my best Spring moves are simply to hold and maintain posture. However, I could move Eastmark City to Eastmark Port just to have a fleet in my port—though this doesn't expand my reach since the port is landlocked-ish.

Actually, looking at adjacency again:
Eastmark City -> ['East Eastmark', 'Eastmark Fort', 'Eastmark Port', 'West Eastmark']
Eastmark Port -> ['Eastmark City', 'West Eastmark']
West Eastmark -> ['Border Delt-East', 'East Deltara', 'Eastmark City', 'Eastmark Port']

So if I moved Eastmark City to Eastmark Port, my port would be occupied. But that puts a unit in a relatively useless position.

Hmm. What if I moved Eastmark City to West Eastmark? Then I could move West Eastmark somewhere else? But West Eastmark can only go to Border Delt-East, East Deltara, Eastmark City, or Eastmark Port. If I move Eastmark City to West Eastmark, then West Eastmark is free to move but still has limited options.

This seems like a lot of shuffling for no gain. Better to simply hold and continue diplomatic efforts.

But I must submit orders. I'll hold all units. It's boring but strategically sound given my commitments and geography.

Wait—I should check if there's any way I can help Grenmar. Core Eastmark is adjacent to Core Fjordland, but that's Grenmar's center now. I could support Grenmar's hold on Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark if there's an attack. Is Avalon attacking Core Fjordland? I don't know. Avalon is far away. Are there any Avalon units adjacent to Core Fjordland? Looking at Avalon's units: ['Avalon City', 'Avalon Port', 'Border Aval-Bore', 'Border Gren-Aval', 'Core Avalon', 'Core Grenmar', 'East Grenmar']. Yes! Avalon has a unit in Core Grenmar. Is Core Grenmar adjacent to Core Fjordland? I don't have the full adjacency map, but based on geography:
- Core Grenmar borders Core Fjordland? Probably, since they're neighboring powers. But actually, in a wheel map, the cores should be in the center. Core Grenmar and Core Fjordland might be adjacent or might not. Let me think about the map structure.

Actually, I don't have adjacencies for provinces outside my home area. I only have adjacency for my units. So I can't definitively say whether Core Grenmar is adjacent to Core Fjordland.

However, Gavin's message from last turn said: "your offer to support Core Fjordland still stands if Avalon shifts west again." This suggests that Avalon might be threatening Core Fjordland or has units that could reach it. If Core Grenmar is adjacent to Core Fjordland, then the Avalon unit there could attack.

If I support Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark, and there's no attack, nothing happens (the support is cut if attacked, but if not attacked it's just a useless order). If there IS an attack, my support defends it. This is a no-risk move that helps an ally.

So I should submit: Core Eastmark supports hold of Core Fjordland.

And hold everything else. This keeps my eastern borders stable, maintains interior strength, and helps Gavin.

Actually wait—can I support a hold on a province I don't know is adjacent? The orders require me to specify a destination. For support hold, the unit being supported just gives the province name. The supporter must be adjacent to that province.

I don't know if Core Eastmark is adjacent to Core Fjordland. Looking at the adjacency list for Core Eastmark: ['Border East-Fjor', 'Core Deltara', 'Core Fjordland'].

YES! Core Eastmark IS adjacent to Core Fjordland! Perfect. So I can support hold of Core Fjordland from Core Eastmark.

I'll do that. It's a meaningful defensive support for Gavin at zero risk to myself.

Other than that, everything holds. This is the progressive foreign policy move: defend allies, maintain agreements, don't start wars.

Let me also send diplomatic messages in this round:

1. To Deltara: Warmly reaffirm the pact now that he's de-escalated.
2. To Fjordland: Note that his march didn't materialize or bounced, but the quiet frontier holds as long as he keeps peace.
3. To Grenmar: Execute the support for Core Fjordland, coordinate further.
4. To Cascadia: Decline to attack Deltara but offer alternative paths.
5. To Avalon: Reject his framing.

Deltara.text: Pete — spheres it is. My west, your east. Don’t test the line and I won’t test yours. I’m not looking over my shoulder if you’re not looking over yours. Let’s keep it that way.

Deltara — I’m hitting Core Borealis from the north this Fall. If you can push Cascadia’s southern line or even feint at West Cascadia, she can’t reinforce the northern fort. Coordinated pressure now could split her defense wide open. What’s your read on her southern flank?

Pete — Eastmark’s western line stays quiet. My attention is north this season, not west. If your front with Cascadia stabilizes, we should talk seriously about Avalon. Seven centers is the real outlier on this board. — AOC

Eastmark.text: AOC — Fjordland’s your fight, not mine. Keep it that way and we stay in our own lanes.

Still holding at four, pushing west this Fall. If you see Avalon start sliding units off his eastern line toward me, that means he’s weakening against your arc. Keep me posted if his posture shifts — the reverse is true for you too.

AOC — I’m in. Four years of clean borders is the foundation of anything larger. I want to extend that indefinitely and explore what a stabilizing alignment looks like. That said, I noticed your unit in West Fjordland — that’s a significant expansion. Is Eastmark drawing Fjordland into a containment effort, or is this opportunistic growth? I’m not judging, but I need to know our shared boundaries before I commit Deltara to a wider partnership. Let’s talk openly about where the eastern line stops.

Fjordland.text: JD — locking this in. I’m hitting Grenmar City from East Grenmar this Fall. If you support that attack from West Grenmar, we take it clean. If you’d rather hit Grenmar Port yourself, say so now and I’ll adjust. But we need to strike the same season and divide his defense. Clock’s ticking. Confirm your angle.

JD — look at your map. Eastmark is in West Fjordland. Grenmar holds Core Fjordland. You’re down to three units defending four centers, and two of your neighbors are eating your territory. If you want to survive as more than a speed bump, you need to pick a side with real leverage. The coalition against Avalon is where the power is. Otherwise you’re fighting for scraps while Rubio wins the board. Your call.
Vance — you left your door unlatched while you threatened your neighbors. I’m securing what you threatened. — AOC

Grenmar.text: Gavin — you want East Grenmar back? Come and try. I’ll be in your capital by winter either way. The only question is how many centers you lose before you accept reality.

Grenmar — a heads-up from the east: Avalon’s home centers at Avalon City and Avalon Fort look lightly held from where I sit. Most of his weight is on the forward edge with me and on your western front. If you press Core Grenmar or Border Gren-Aval hard, he has to pull from somewhere. Consider it.

Gavin — straight answer: I cannot hit Core Avalon or Border Aval-Bore from Deltara. Geography doesn’t allow it. My western units are securing my frontier with Cascadia, not staging for a trans-continental strike. What I can do is support pressure on Avalon's northwestern arc if Borealis or Cascadia opens that lane. If you have a specific, reachable target you need supported, name it. Otherwise, keep me posted on your southeastern push against East Grenmar — I’ll coordinate where I can.

Gavin — I’m not feinting. I have a unit in West Fjordland and I’m pressing his home territory this Fall. Expect Vance’s entire front to snap eastward. Use the window to retake West Grenmar or push deeper. Let’s coordinate next season. — AOC

press.text: Buttigieg — nice try clawing back to seven, but you’re still squatting on Cascadian soil. I’m fortifying every inch of sovereign territory this Spring. Come at me and you’ll bounce off a wall of American steel. You can have a border freeze when you return Core Cascadia — until then, patriots don’t negotiate with trespassers. — President Greene

AOC — Pete’s back to seven centers while you play footsie with Fjordland. Real power would be driving a spear into his eastern flank before he turns the whole wheel into one Beltway bureaucracy. Push west now, or don’t pretend later that you weren’t warned. — Greene

Independent — I’ve got Core Borealis and I’m not leaving. Touch it and you’ll find out what happens to globalist lapdogs who bite the hand that feeds them peace. Focus on Avalon, not Cascadia. — President Greene

Rubio — seven centers and still reaching. I’m locking down my house. Point your ambitions at Grenmar and Fjordland. Trespass on Cascadian soil and I’ll make sure those seven centers cost you everything. — Greene

Deltara here. I’m prepared to coordinate pressure on Cascadia this Spring—either supporting a move into Core Borealis or pinning her southern line so she can’t reinforce. Before I commit, I need clarity: what is your exact Fall plan, and are you open to a hard non-aggression understanding between our blocs through Year 8? I’m not interested in bleeding strength for a one-time favor. If we partner, it needs to be durable.

Marco — noted. I’m consolidating my own frontier this season with no moves into your sphere. If you keep your side of the line, I’ll keep mine. Let’s not make each other the problem while the clock runs down.

AOC — I share your concern about the board’s balance, and I value our clean border. The reality is geographic: Deltara’s western units are committed this Spring. I can’t launch a cross-map strike while my own flank is contested. Once that line is stable, I’m open to a concrete, coordinated containment plan. What specific moves are you envisioning? If it’s realistic, I’ll calibrate Fall timing to support it.

President Greene — I offered you a negotiated settlement and you chose escalation. Now your position is four centers with two powers pressing. You still have an off-ramp: recognize the border at Border Casc-Delt, withdraw from Core Borealis, and keep your home territory intact. Deltara prefers order to attrition, but we are prepared to defend our position if forced. The choice is yours.

Pete — seven and seven. You’re not a bystander, you’re a co-leader. The ‘coalition’ you’re flirting with is a knife that cuts both ways — the moment you help them bring me down, they turn on you next. I’m open to a genuine understanding of mutual restraint, but I’m not going to unilaterally disarm while you posture. If you want peace, define your borders and stick to them. If you want war, pick your side and accept the consequences. No more vague threats.

AOC — you want to organize a coalition? Fine. But marches have a way of turning into routs when the target doesn’t fold. I’ve got seven centers and a compact interior. You’ve got five and a unit in Fjordland’s backyard. Ask yourself who bleeds first when this kicks off. If you’re smart, you’ll keep your powder dry and let Deltara do the heavy lifting. If you’re not, you’ll find out why Avalon doesn’t lose multi-front wars.

Gavin — East Grenmar is a mistake. I’m giving you one chance: pull that unit back to your interior this Spring, or I treat it as an act of war and remove it by Fall. I’ve got better things to do than grind you into dust, but I will if you force my hand. You’ve got four centers; act like you want to keep them.

JD — Eastmark is sitting in West Fjordland. That’s your home turf, not mine. If you want my attention focused west, you need to give me a reason. Otherwise, I might find it more useful to let the eastern powers bleed each other while I finish my own business. Your call.
President Greene — Deltara just clawed back to seven. How many of those were yours? You’re bleeding northern centers while warning me about borders. I’m not your problem; Pete is. Wake up.
Stay west of West Borealis. I’m not asking.

Pete — fair question, and I’ll answer it straight. West Fjordland is not expansionist opportunism; it’s a direct consequence of Vance threatening Border East-Fjor two years in a row and then digging into West Grenmar. Eastmark stepped up to relieve pressure on an ally and protect our own frontier. My boundary with Deltara hasn’t moved, and it won’t. What I want to talk about now is Avalon—seven centers, consolidating the western hemisphere, and happily watching the rest of us skirmish. If Eastmark and Deltara are serious about a stabilizing partnership, I think we formalize it: mutual non-aggression between us, joint commitment to cap unilateral expansion, and information-sharing on Avalon’s posture. No treaty of aggression—just a solid understanding that neither of us goes to eighteen alone. Are you open to that conversation? — AOC

President Vance — my unit is in West Fjordland because you spent two seasons threatening Border East-Fjor and then pivoted to attack Grenmar. That’s not Eastmark aggression; that’s Eastmark refusing to be a doormat. Here’s the off-ramp: pull back from West Grenmar, stop probing my frontier, and I’ll stop pressing yours. De-escalation saves both our peoples from a war neither of us can afford while Avalon sits at seven centers. — AOC

Gavin — my attack on Fjordland City bounced last Fall. Vance is dug in. But he can’t cover two fronts forever. Are you positioned to hit him from Core Fjordland or West Grenmar this Spring? If we coordinate a two-way squeeze—me pressing east, you pressing west—we might finally crack his shell and give both our nations room to breathe. What do your orders look like? — AOC

Marco — lane discipline acknowledged. But seven centers is a lot of lane. I’m not looking for a collision, but I am looking for proof that Avalon’s growth stops before it swallows the western hemisphere. Keep it south of your own core for a season or two, and the eastern arc stays quiet. Push deeper into Borealis or Grenmar, and the coalition solidifies against you. Your move. — AOC

President Greene — Deltara pulled back from 7 to 6 and now sits at 7 again. That’s not runaway expansion; that’s stabilization. Avalon at 7 with three foreign cores is the structural threat. If you want to coordinate real containment, Eastmark is willing to work with you on a northern brake. But I’m done being your proxy against a neighbor who’s kept his word with me. Target the actual hegemon or stop wasting my time. — AOC

Borealis — you’re recovering. Good. Avalon’s watching your western flank. If you need an eastern voice backing your independence, you’ve got one. Eastmark’s coalition is forming; you’re welcome in it. — AOC

Avalon — message received and understood. I’m turning my full weight west this season to reclaim Core Borealis. No eastward probe from me. Let’s keep the Aval-Bore line quiet while you handle Grenmar and I handle Cascadia.

Cascadia — you’re holding four centers with two empty home provinces and Deltara at your throat. I’m stepping into East Borealis this spring and I intend to reclaim Core Borealis. Vacate it and I stop there; force me to fight for it and I’ll coordinate with Deltara to erase your northern flank entirely. Pragmatism or oblivion. Choose by Fall.

Deltara — Cascadia is folds. I’m pushing into East Borealis to pressure her rear and retake Core Borealis. If you keep the southern pressure on, she has to split her four units across two fronts. We box her out without ever needing to trust each other. Just stay out of my way in the north.

Eastmark — four centers and still kicking. I’m consolidating west to take back Core Borealis this year. If Avalon shifts any weight southward off his eastern line, I’d like a heads-up. Likewise, I’ll flag anything that looks like it’s heading your way.

Gavin — Avalon just offered me joint action against you. I haven't said yes yet. Here's my price for saying no: your unit vacates Core Fjordland this Fall. I walk in, it's my center, and I stop pressing your western flank. Refuse, and I throw West Grenmar behind Avalon's City assault and we carve your nation up between us. You're a 4-center power with two hungry neighbors. Pick survival or extinction.

Marco — one more invitation and no meat. I supported nothing last season, and nothing changed. Here's the deal: if you're serious about a western carve-up, show me your army movements first. I want to see East Grenmar and Core Grenmar both committed against Grenmar's home centers before I risk a unit on your word. When I see pressure, I'll add mine. Not before. Fjordland doesn't fight other people's battles on a handshake.

AOC — West Fjordland was a provocative move. Hear this clearly: that unit stays put this Fall, or the next season becomes a total war on your eastern border regardless of what it costs me. I will burn my own economy to make sure you don't sleep. Hold the line and we both survive; push deeper and we both bleed out while Rubio and Buttigieg lap up what's left. Your call.

Pete — two years of 'coalition' talk and you're still at the same score. I've reached my limit. Are you hitting Avalon this Fall or not? I need a straight answer and a straight plan: which unit, which province, which season. If you're not moving against him, stop messaging me about containment until you've actually contained something.

AOC — we’re in the home stretch. Our border stays clean, as promised. If Avalon makes a play that unbalances the board in Fall, I want to know we can trust each other to respond proportionally. Not looking for anything rash, just clarity: if the final turn turns chaotic, Deltara and Eastmark stay aligned.

President Greene — I’ve held my position and not pressed further into Cascadia’s home territory. You’re at four centers with two fronts. A final-season gamble against a fortified Deltara line won’t give you what you want, but it will cost you what you have. I’m offering the same border freeze I proposed last year. Take it, and we both survive the finish.

Marco — Deltara’s not moving against you this Spring. I intend to hold my line and let the season resolve. If you’re thinking about a late push, remember the coalition math. A sprint to eight or nine centers just paints a target for Fall. Prudent restraint serves us both.

JD — I told you the truth: Deltara cannot strike Avalon from our current position without overextending. That hasn’t changed. What has changed is that the final turns are here. If you want containment to mean something, hold your ground and don’t let Grenmar collapse. I’ll keep my border quiet and my forces ready. That’s what I can do.

To all — President Greene, Cascadia. It’s Fall Year 8. I’m finishing on my terms. Anyone who thinks they’ll walk into Cascadian ground is about to find a locked door and a loaded cannon. Merry Christmas. — Greene

Gavin — Year 8, clock's running out. I need Core Fjordland, you need Avalon off your back. Here's the trade: your unit vacates Core Fjordland this Spring, ceding it to me. In exchange, West Grenmar pulls back to Border Fjor-Gren immediately after, and I spend my Fall striking at Avalon's flank instead of yours. Your eastern border rests, your western border rests, and you live to see the endgame. Occupation ends with a handshake, not a war. What's it going to be?

Marco — if you're not going to coordinate against Grenmar, then stop messaging me about joint action. Fjordland fights its own battles. But hear this: if I see Avalon units pushing any closer to my frontier, I'll make sure every Grenmar unit that's not facing you is facing Deltara instead. Keep your distance, and I keep mine.

AOC — you crossed into West Fjordland. That's a provocation I haven't answered yet. I'm choosing restraint because the real threat is the 7-center powers. But if your unit moves one inch closer to Fjordland City or Port, I unleash everything on your eastern border. Stay put in West Fjordland and we both survive this. Push again and we both go down fighting.

Pete — two turns. You're tied with Avalon. If you don't make a decisive play against him now, you risk a 7-7 tie that helps nobody. I'm not asking to join your coalition — I'm telling you to use it. Put pressure on his Cascadian flank so he's looking over both shoulders. That's how Deltara wins, not by waiting for geography to change.

Marco — here we go. You wanted a two-front war. I'm taking Core Grenmar and Border Gren-Aval simultaneously this Spring. You can hold both, one, or neither — but you can't do it without stripping your northern defenses against Deltara. Every unit you pull to stop me is a unit Pete eats. Your choice. — Gavin

Cascadia — I'm consolidating this Spring: holding Border Bore-Casc and rotating a unit to East Borealis to secure my interior corridor. I'm not stepping into Core Borealis. You've got Deltara bearing down on your southern flank; don't waste strength north when your real fight is behind you. — Borealis

Deltara — I'm staging a unit to East Borealis this Spring to set up a supported push into Cascadia's rear in Fall. Keep her southern line hot and she won't be able to reinforce the north. If she splits, one of us cracks through. — Borealis
Avalon — my eastern line is quiet this Spring. West Borealis stays in place and I'm not probing Aval-Bore. Keep your attention where it matters and I'll do the same. — Borealis

Eastmark — holding and consolidating this Spring to set up one last push in Fall. If you see Avalon shift west off his Grenmar line, flag me; he's the only power who could still ruin my day. — Borealis

Deltara.press:
We’re in the final phase of the game. My reasoning as Pete Buttigieg is the same as before: I need to be diplomatic, build coalitions, and position for the endgame. With only two moves left (Spring and Fall Year 8), I can’t afford to make a fatal error. I’ll message key players to solidify my position.

**Spring Year 8 reasoning:**

We’re in the final stretch. My position is stable at 7 centers, tied with Avalon. The key variables are the western and eastern fronts. I need to reassure allies, deter threats, and position for the Fall phase where the game ends. I’ll send brief, direct messages to ensure my allies hold and my enemies hesitate.

- **Borealis — Confirm the alliance** and coordinate any last-minute pressure on Avalon or Cascadia.
- **Eastmark — Lock in the non-aggression pact** and see if she’ll commit to a joint stance against Avalon if needed.
- **Cascadia — Firm but calm deterrence** to keep her from gambling on a final push.
- **Avalon — Signal that I’m not the threat**; if he overextends elsewhere, he risks a coalition.
- **Fjordland — Brief update** to keep him from panicking or attacking the wrong target.

I’ll skip Grenmar unless needed; he’s contained and not a priority.
Deltara.orders:
We are at Spring Year 8, the penultimate phase. After this Fall, the game ends at 8 years. The final score will be based on centers owned after Fall Year 8. Currently, Avalon has 7 centers, Deltara has 7, Eastmark 5, Fjordland 4, Grenmar 4, Borealis 4, Cascadia 4.

The only way to win is to be solo at 18 (impossible now) or have the most centers after Fall Year 8. So every center counts. I need to think about what can realistically change in these last two phases.

Key facts:
- I have 7 centers, all occupied by my 7 units.
- Avalon also has 7.
- To win, I need to either gain a center and hope Avalon doesn't, or at least not lose any.

Let's look at my position and possible moves.

Adjacency:
- Border Casc-Delt -> Core Cascadia, East Cascadia, West Deltara
- Border Delt-East -> Core Deltara, East Deltara, West Eastmark
- Core Cascadia -> Border Casc-Delt, Core Borealis, Core Deltara
- Core Deltara -> Border Delt-East, Core Cascadia, Core Eastmark
- Deltara City -> Deltara Fort, Deltara Port, East Deltara, West Deltara
- Deltara Port -> Deltara City, West Deltara
- West Deltara -> Border Casc-Delt, Deltara City, Deltara Port, East Cascadia

I have a unit in every one of my 7 centers. Every center is occupied. Good.

Now, what can I attack?
- From Core Cascadia, I can move to Core Borealis (but it's occupied by Cascadia) or Core Deltara (occupied by me).
- From Core Deltara, I can move to Core Eastmark (occupied by Eastmark) or Core Cascadia (occupied by me) or Border Delt-East (occupied by me).
- From Border Casc-Delt, I can move to Core Cascadia (occupied by me) or East Cascadia (occupied by Cascadia).
- From West Deltara, I can move to East Cascadia (occupied by Cascadia).
- From Border Delt-East, I can move to Core Deltara (occupied by me) or West Eastmark (occupied by Eastmark).

So the only enemy-occupied provinces adjacent to my units are:
- Core Borealis (adjacent to Core Cascadia) — occupied by Cascadia
- East Cascadia (adjacent to Border Casc-Delt and West Deltara) — occupied by Cascadia
- West Eastmark (adjacent to Border Delt-East) — occupied by Eastmark

I could potentially take one of these. But which one is realistic?

Attacking Eastmark would violate 4+ years of trust and likely result in me being attacked back by a 5-center power plus potentially others. And I might not even succeed if she defends.

Attacking Cascadia: Core Borealis or East Cascadia. Cascadia is at 4 centers. If I attack, I might succeed or bounce. But if I attack Cascadia now, I might trigger a desperate retaliation.

However, Borealis says he is staging to East Borealis to push into Cascadia's rear in Fall. If I coordinate with Borealis, we could both hit Cascadia in Fall and potentially split her centers.

But wait — it's Spring now. I need to submit Spring orders. Then there will be a Fall phase. In Spring, if I move into a center, I don't own it until after Fall. So the key is Fall Year 8.

But for now, Spring Year 8 moves set up Fall.

Let's think about what to do in Spring.

Option 1: All holds. Safe, but passive.
Option 2: Move to set up a Fall attack.
Option 3: Move to a more defensible position.

Avalon and I are tied at 7. If neither of us gains, we tie. But the goal is to WIN, not tie (though a tie might mean I win if I'm first alphabetically or something? The rules say "most centers after 8 years" — ties are possible).

But Pete Buttigieg wants to win. What would pragmatic Pete do?

He has built trust with Eastmark. He has been firm but not reckless. But now, with the game on the line, would he stab Eastmark to get to 8?

Looking at Eastmark's position: she has units in Border East-Fjor, Core Eastmark, East Eastmark, Eastmark City, West Eastmark. So West Eastmark is occupied. If I attack from Border Delt-East to West Eastmark with support, that's strength 2 vs her 1 (if she holds). I'd take it in Fall.

But what are the consequences? She might attack back from West Eastmark to Border Delt-East, cutting my support. But if she's been true to her word for 4 years, she might not expect it. This is the classic endgame stab.

However, as Pete Buttigieg — pragmatic, trustworthy, data-driven, steady — would he stab his most reliable ally in the final turn? That's a tough question. In Diplomacy, endgame stabs are common. But Pete's persona is about credibility and not governing by overreach. Breaking a 4-year pact for one center might be "crisis politics" that he claims to reject.

On the other hand, winning the game is the objective. A pragmatic moderate might calculate that defeating Avalon is impossible due to geography, but Eastmark is adjacent and vulnerable.

Wait — actually, attacking Eastmark doesn't help me if she retaliates. And she has 5 units. If I take West Eastmark, I get 8 centers. But if she takes Border Delt-East back, I stay at 7. Net zero unless I can hold both.

Let's calculate: If I move Border Delt-East -> West Eastmark (supported by Core Deltara), and Eastmark holds West Eastmark, that's 2 vs 1, I take it. But then in Fall, I'd need to hold it. Eastmark could attack back with multiple units. But she can only attack from Core Eastmark (adjacent to West Eastmark? Let's check. Core Eastmark -> ... actually from the list: Core Eastmark's adjacencies aren't shown, but West Eastmark is adjacent to Border Delt-East and East Deltara. That's all I know. If West Eastmark is attacked, who can support its hold? Core Eastmark might be adjacent. Or other units. But Eastmark has 5 units.

Wait, this is risky. And it would destroy my relationship with Eastmark for one center.

What about Cascadia? She has 4 centers. If I attack East Cascadia from West Deltara (supported by Border Casc-Delt or Core Cascadia), that's 2 vs 1. But then I'd lose Core Cascadia or Border Casc-Delt if she counter-attacks. Hmm.

Actually, Borealis is threatening Cascadia from the north. If I join in, Cascadia has to defend on two fronts. But I already have 7 centers tied for first. If I can take one from Cascadia and not lose any, I get to 8 and probably win. But if Avalon also gets to 8, we tie.

What's Avalon doing? Avalon is at 7, with units in Border Aval-Bore, Border Gren-Aval, Core Avalon, Core Grenmar, East Avalon, East Grenmar, West Avalon. He could potentially take more from Borealis, Grenmar, or Fjordland.

Fjordland is at 4, Grenmar at 4, Borealis at 4. Avalon could expand.

So to win, I likely need to expand too.

Cascadia at 4 is the softest target adjacent to me. But she says she's "massing every gun" and "finishing on her terms." She might defend heavily on her southern front because she doesn't trust me.

However, let's look at Cascadia's actual units: Cascadia City, Core Borealis, East Cascadia, West Cascadia. So East Cascadia is occupied. Core Borealis is occupied. If I attack East Cascadia with 2 strength, and she holds with 1, I take it. But if she moves from Cascadia City to support East Cascadia, it's 2 vs 2, bounce.

Or, she might attack INTO my territory. From East Cascadia, she can attack Core Cascadia or Border Casc-Delt. So she might be aggressive.

If I support-hold Core Cascadia with Core Deltara, and move Border Casc-Delt to support an attack on East Cascadia... but Border Casc-Delt is one of my centers. If I move it away, I lose the center unless I occupy it later. But in Spring, if I move Border Casc-Delt to East Cascadia (attack), then Border Casc-Delt becomes empty. If she doesn't move into it, I lose it after Fall if it's unoccupied. Wait — centers you occupy become yours after Fall. If I move out of Border Casc-Delt in Spring, and don't occupy it in Fall, I lose it at the end of the year. That would be terrible.

So I cannot move out of Border Casc-Delt unless I plan to reoccupy it in Fall, or I accept losing the center. Since there are only two phases left, moving out of a center in Spring means it's empty for Fall. Unless I move back in Fall — but then I waste two seasons.

So I probably should not move out of any of my 7 centers unless I want to trade centers.

Actually, I could move from Core Cascadia (which is a center I own) to attack Core Borealis. Then Core Cascadia would be empty. I'd need to reoccupy it. But why? Core Borealis is Cascadia's center.

Or I could move from Core Deltara to attack Core Eastmark. Then Core Deltara is empty. Not good.

So to expand while keeping my 7 centers, I need to use my border units that are on the edges but not in centers? Wait, all my units ARE in centers. So any move out of a center leaves it empty.

Unless... I use a unit that is not in a center to attack, but all my units are in centers.

So any attack risks losing a center.

For example, if I move Border Casc-Delt (my center) to East Cascadia to attack, and move West Deltara to Border Casc-Delt to backfill, and move... wait, that could work:
- West Deltara -> Border Casc-Delt (backfill, so Border Casc-Delt stays occupied)
- Border Casc-Delt -> East Cascadia (attack with 1)
- But I need support for this attack to succeed. Core Cascadia could support Border Casc-Delt -> East Cascadia. But Core Cascadia would then be holding.

Actually, Core Cascadia is adjacent to Border Casc-Delt? No. Core Cascadia is adjacent to Border Casc-Delt (yes, from the list: "Core Cascadia -> ['Border Casc-Delt', 'Core Borealis', 'Core Deltara']"). So Core Cascadia supports Border Casc-Delt -> East Cascadia? No, you must be adjacent to the destination to support a move. Core Cascadia is NOT adjacent to East Cascadia. From the list, Core Cascadia -> Border Casc-Delt, Core Borealis, Core Deltara. So Core Cascadia cannot support an attack on East Cascadia.

Who is adjacent to East Cascadia? Border Casc-Delt and West Deltara (and also East Borealis? wait, no). Let me check:
- Border Casc-Delt -> ['Core Cascadia', 'East Cascadia', 'West Deltara']
- West Deltara -> ['Border Casc-Delt', 'Deltara City', 'Deltara Port', 'East Cascadia']

So both Border Casc-Delt and West Deltara are adjacent to East Cascadia. So if both attack East Cascadia, that's strength 2. But if both move out, then Border Casc-Delt and West Deltara become empty! I would need to fill them.

West Deltara is not a supply center, so losing the unit there isn't a supply center loss. Border Casc-Delt IS a supply center, so I cannot leave it empty.

Option:
- Border Casc-Delt holds (or supports an attack), staying in place.
- West Deltara -> East Cascadia (attack, supported by Border Casc-Delt). But Border Casc-Delt is adjacent to East Cascadia, so yes, Border Casc-Delt can support West Deltara -> East Cascadia.

But if West Deltara moves to East Cascadia, and East Cascadia is occupied by Cascadia, and I have support from Border Casc-Delt, that's strength 2. If Cascadia holds or moves with 1 support, it's a bounce. If she only holds with 1, I win.

Then West Deltara becomes empty. But West Deltara is not a supply center, so I don't lose a center. However, the province becomes empty. Deltara Port is adjacent to West Deltara, and Deltara City is also adjacent. I could move Deltara Port -> West Deltara to backfill, but Deltara Port would leave Deltara City... no wait, Deltara Port is a separate unit. If Deltara Port moves to West Deltara, Deltara Port province becomes empty, which is fine (not a center). Deltara City can hold.

Wait, actually, the only centers I need to keep occupied are: Border Casc-Delt, Border Delt-East, Core Cascadia, Core Deltara, Deltara City, Deltara Fort, Deltara Port. If West Deltara is not a center, moving out of it is fine from a supply perspective.

Let's check the supply center list for Deltara:
centers(7) ['Border Casc-Delt', 'Border Delt-East', 'Core Cascadia', 'Core Deltara', 'Deltara City', 'Deltara Fort', 'Deltara Port']

Yes, West Deltara and East Deltara are NOT supply centers. They are interior provinces. So I can safely move units through them without losing centers.

So a possible attack sequence:
- West Deltara -> East Cascadia
- Border Casc-Delt supports West Deltara -> East Cascadia (strength 2)
- Border Delt-East holds
- Core Deltara holds
- Core Cascadia holds
- Deltara City holds
- Deltara Port holds

This leaves West Deltara empty, which is fine. After Spring, I'd have a unit in East Cascadia (if it succeeds) or bounced back to West Deltara (if it fails). In Fall, if I took East Cascadia, I just hold it. If bounced, I might move back or try again.

But wait — if West Deltara moves to East Cascadia, and Cascadia also moves East Cascadia -> West Deltara (a swap? no, they can't swap). Or she could attack from East Cascadia to Border Casc-Delt, cutting my support! If she attacks Border Casc-Delt from East Cascadia, that cuts my support unless Border Casc-Delt is supported. But if Border Casc-Delt is using its order to support, it can't support itself.

If Cascadia attacks Border Casc-Delt from East Cascadia, and I have no support for Border Casc-Delt, then Border Casc-Delt might be dislodged if the attack has strength > 1 (or even 1, since support cuts don't reduce the hold strength unless the unit is dislodged?). Wait, in Diplomacy, if a unit is attacked, its support is cut, but the unit itself still defends with strength 1 (unless dislodged by a unit with greater strength). So if Cascadia moves East Cascadia -> Border Casc-Delt with strength 1, and Border Casc-Delt is supporting (not holding), its support is cut but it still defends at strength 1. So East Cascadia attacking with 1 vs Border Casc-Delt defending at 1 = bounce. Border Casc-Delt stays in place.

But wait, if my support is cut, the attack on East Cascadia is only strength 1 (West Deltara alone). If East Cascadia holds, it's 1 vs 1 = bounce. So neither move succeeds.

However, if Cascadia does NOT attack Border Casc-Delt, then my attack is 2 vs her hold of 1, and I take East Cascadia. And her attack on Border Casc-Delt fails because it's 1 vs 1.

So the success depends on her actions.

Alternatively, I could be more conservative and just hold everything, ensuring I keep my 7 centers and hope Avalon doesn't expand either.

Let's think about what Avalon can do. He has units in East Avalon, West Avalon, Border Aval-Bore, Border Gren-Aval, Core Avalon, Core Grenmar, East Grenmar. He could potentially:
- Take East Borealis from Borealis?
- Take something from Grenmar? But Grenmar has only 4 centers and they seem locked in a stalemate.
- Take something from Fjordland? Fjordland is at 4 and has been fighting Grenmar and Eastmark.

Actually, Avalon might not be able to expand easily either, because he's also fully extended.

But Borealis says he's going to attack Cascadia's rear. That doesn't directly help or hurt me.

What about Eastmark? She has 5 centers and a unit in West Fjordland. She seems to be fighting Fjordland, not me. She has been a reliable partner. Stabbing her would be out of character for Pete Buttigieg, and risky.

What about attacking Core Eastmark from Core Deltara? Core Deltara is adjacent to Core Eastmark (from the list: Core Deltara -> ['Border Delt-East', 'Core Cascadia', 'Core Eastmark']). So I could attack Core Eastmark from Core Deltara, supported by... who? Border Delt-East is adjacent to West Eastmark, not Core Eastmark. East Deltara is not a unit I have anymore. So I can only attack Core Eastmark with 1 strength. That's unlikely to succeed.

What about attacking Core Borealis from Core Cascadia? With support from... nobody adjacent to Core Borealis except Core Cascadia. So only 1 strength. And Core Borealis is occupied by Cascadia, who likely defends.

So the only viable attack with support is East Cascadia via West Deltara + Border Casc-Delt support.

Would Pete do it? He's pragmatic. He wants to win. The clock is running out. Cascadia has been threatening him for years and refused every olive branch. Taking East Cascadia would give him 8 centers and probably the win if Avalon can't expand. It would also be a "measured" response to her threats — taking her frontier unit, not her home centers.

But East Cascadia might not be a supply center! Let's check Cascadia's centers: ['Cascadia City', 'Cascadia Fort', 'Cascadia Port', 'Core Borealis']. So East Cascadia is NOT a supply center! It's just a province. Taking East Cascadia wouldn't give me a center, just a position.

Oh no! That's critical. The supply centers Cascadia owns are: Cascadia City, Cascadia Fort, Cascadia Port, Core Borealis, and possibly Border Bore-Casc? Wait, looking at Cascadia's centers list:
centers(4) ['Cascadia City', 'Cascadia Fort', 'Cascadia Port', 'Core Borealis']

And units: ['Cascadia City', 'Core Borealis', 'East Cascadia', 'West Cascadia']

So Cascadia has four centers: City, Fort, Port, and Core Borealis. East Cascadia and West Cascadia are not supply centers.

So if I take East Cascadia, I gain zero supply centers. It would just bounce one of her units. That's pointless for the endgame.

What about Core Borealis? It's a supply center, occupied by Cascadia. If I attack it from Core Cascadia, that's 1 strength. She probably holds with 1. Bounce.

What about Border Bore-Casc? Wait, Borealis shows: centers(4) ['Border Bore-Casc', 'Borealis City', 'Borealis Fort', 'Borealis Port']. And units: ['Border Bore-Casc', 'Borealis City', 'Borealis Port', 'West Borealis']. So Borealis owns Border Bore-Casc.

Cascadia has Border Bore-Casc? No, looking back: Cascadia's centers are only 4.

So the unowned centers list is empty — all 35 are taken. To gain a center, I must conquer one.

The centers adjacent to me and owned by others:
- Core Borealis (owned by Cascadia) — adjacent to Core Cascadia
- Core Eastmark (owned by Eastmark) — adjacent to Core Deltara
- East Cascadia (not a center)
- West Eastmark (not a center? Let's check Eastmark's centers: ['Border East-Fjor', 'Core Eastmark', 'Eastmark City', 'Eastmark Fort', 'Eastmark Port']. So West Eastmark is NOT a center.

Wait, so even if I take West Eastmark, I don't gain a center! It's just a province.

To actually gain a center from Eastmark, I'd need to take Border East-Fjor or Core Eastmark. Core Eastmark is adjacent to Core Deltara. Border East-Fjor is NOT adjacent to me.

So the only enemy supply center I am adjacent to is:
- Core Borealis (Cascadia)
- Core Eastmark (Eastmark)

And I can only attack each with 1 strength (no adjacent support possible for those destinations). So I cannot realistically take a center in one phase without a very lucky break (enemy moves out).

Wait, could I support an attack on Core Eastmark? Core Deltara is adjacent to Core Eastmark. Can any other unit support from Core Deltara? The support would need to come from a unit adjacent to Core Eastmark. Is Border Delt-East adjacent to Core Eastmark? No, Border Delt-East -> Core Deltara, East Deltara, West Eastmark. Not Core Eastmark. Is Core Cascadia adjacent to Core Eastmark? No.

So only Core Deltara can attack Core Eastmark, with 1 strength.

Similarly, only Core Cascadia can attack Core Borealis, with 1 strength.

So I physically CANNOT conquer a center this turn with a supported attack! Unless the enemy leaves it empty.

Given this, any aggressive move is likely to be a bounce or a retreat, and risks leaving my provinces empty or vulnerable.

Therefore, the pragmatic move is to hold everything, defend my 7 centers, and hope that Avalon also cannot expand (or that I can out-tie him).

But wait — Avalon is at 7 centers too. Can he expand? Let's check Avalon's adjacencies:
- Avalon City: adjacent to Avalon Fort, Avalon Port, Core Avalon (all his)
- Avalon Port: adjacent to West Avalon, Core Avalon (his? no, Core Avalon is his center)
- Border Aval-Bore: adjacent to Core Avalon, East Avalon, East Borealis? Actually, check. Border Aval-Bore is between Avalon and Borealis.
- Border Gren-Aval: between Grenmar and Avalon.
- Core Avalon: his center
- Core Grenmar: his center
- East Avalon, East Grenmar, West Avalon: provinces.

What centers does Avalon border? Borealis has Border Bore-Casc (not adjacent to Avalon). But Avalon might have Border Aval-Bore as a center, so he's on Borealis' border. From Border Aval-Bore, he can move to... the center list says unowned is empty, but we need to see the adjacency. Since it's not shown, I'll infer. Avalon might be able to attack Borealis' centers.

Actually, looking at Avalon's units: he has Border Aval-Bore, which is a center he owns. He could move from there to attack Borealis' Borealis City? Not sure.

Alternatively, Avalon could attack Grenmar or Fjordland. Fjordland has 4 units and 4 centers. Avalon has East Grenmar adjacent to... Core Grenmar (his own center). He might be adjacent to Grenmar City.

In any case, I cannot reliably gain a center. So my best bet is to not lose any, maintain my 7, and see if the game ends in a tie or if someone else collapses allowing me a walk-in.

But if I hold everything, I end with 7. If Avalon holds everything, he ends with 7. It's a tie.

If I want to win, I need to either hope Avalon loses a center (unlikely if he's not attacked), or I need to gain one.

Wait — I have 7 units and 7 centers. I cannot build. But I could move a unit to an empty enemy center if they vacate it. But no one is going to vacate a center in the final year unless they're forced.

Unless Borealis attacks Core Borealis (which Cascadia owns) and Cascadia moves out to attack me? That's possible but unlikely.

Actually, here's a thought: What if I support Borealis' attack? If Borealis moves from West Borealis or Border Bore-Casc into Core Borealis, and I support from Core Cascadia... but Core Cascadia is not adjacent to Core Borealis? Wait, yes it is: Core Cascadia -> Border Casc-Delt, Core Borealis, Core Deltara. So Core Cascadia IS adjacent to Core Borealis. So I could support an attack into Core Borealis from Core Cascadia!

If Borealis attacks Core Borealis, and I support with Core Cascadia, that's strength 2. If Cascadia defends with 1, Borealis takes it. But then Borealis gets the center, not me. That doesn't help me win; it helps Borealis.

Alternatively, I could attack Core Borealis myself, supported by... nobody else is adjacent. So 1 strength.

What about a more creative move? Could I move Core Deltara to Core Eastmark and hope Eastmark moves out? If AOC has been reliable, she likely holds her centers. But she has 5 centers and 5 units. If she doesn't expect an attack, she might hold elsewhere. But Core Eastmark is deep in her territory. She probably defends it.

Given the impossibility of reliable conquest, the pragmatic Buttigieg move is to HOLD everything, preserve the tie at worst, and avoid any risks that could drop me below 7. Stabbing AOC would be morally out of character AND tactically pointless (since I'd likely bounce and lose the friendship for nothing).
